metadata.title: Parametric felid body-of-revolution surface profile for the Pass 3 P1 finite-element Laplace-Beltrami solver
metadata.honesty_statement: This is NOT a photogrammetric body scan. It is a parametric surrogate surface of revolution whose axial radius profile is interpolated from the control knots below. The knots encode approximate adult Panthera pardus proportions (head-body length, tail length, torso depth, tail base and tip radii) and are intended to be replaced by a triangulated photogrammetric mesh in a later pass. All quantities are dimensionless ratios of the head-body length (HBL).

sources.citation: Stein AB, Hayssen V (2013). Panthera pardus (Carnivora: Felidae). Mammalian Species 45(900):30-48.
sources.used_for: Approximate adult head-body length (about 0.9-1.9 m) and tail length (about 0.6-1.1 m) ranges; tail/HBL ratio ~0.7 adopted here.

sources.citation: Dziuk G (1988). Finite elements for the Beltrami operator on arbitrary surfaces. In: Partial Differential Equations and Calculus of Variations, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1357:142-155. Springer.
sources.used_for: P1 (linear) surface finite-element discretization of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on a triangulated surface.

sources.citation: Pinkall U, Polthier K (1993). Computing discrete minimal surfaces and their conjugates. Experimental Mathematics 2(1):15-36.
sources.used_for: Cotangent-weight formula for the P1 stiffness matrix: K_ij = -(cot alpha_ij + cot beta_ij) / 2.

sources.citation: Dziuk G, Elliott CM (2013). Finite element methods for surface PDEs. Acta Numerica 22:289-396.
sources.used_for: Lumped-mass surface FEM and implicit-in-diffusion time stepping for reaction-diffusion on surfaces.

sources.citation: Liu RT, Liaw SS, Maini PK (2006). Two-stage Turing model for generating pigment patterns on the leopard and the jaguar. Physical Review E 74(1):011914.
sources.used_for: Two-stage protocol: the saturated Stage-1 spot field is the initial condition of a Stage-2 integration on the grown (adult) domain.

surface_of_revolution.coordinate_system: Axis x runs from the neck (x = 0) through the torso to the tail tip; r(x) is the local radius. Both are in units of the head-body length HBL; the mesh is scaled so that the Stage-1 (cub) critical Turing wavelength lambda_c is 1 mesh unit.
surface_of_revolution.notes: Torso radius 0.10 HBL (chest depth ~0.2 HBL), tail base radius 0.020 HBL and tail tip radius 0.004 HBL (about 1 cm diameter on a 1.3 m leopard) are assumed adult proportions, not measured on the specimen; the tail taper is linear in x between the base and tip knots. In cub-wavelength units (HBL = 22) the tail runs from r = 0.44 to r = 0.088, straddling both Murray thresholds: r_crit = 1/sqrt(k_+^2 - k_c^2) = 0.29 (fastest-growing mode becomes the m = 0 ring) and r_excl = 1/k_+ = 0.14 (circumference < lambda_+: every m >= 1 mode, including the axially uniform n = 0 longitudinal-stripe mode, leaves the Turing band).

two_stage_growth.protocol: Stage 1 integrates the Thomas kinetics on the cub body (geometry scaled by 1/G, i.e. lumped mass scaled by 1/G^2 with scale-invariant cotangent stiffness) to a saturated spot pre-pattern; Stage 2 continues from that field on the adult body (G = growth_factor) so that each Stage-1 spot is G times larger than the adult wavelength and reorganizes into a ring/rosette.
two_stage_growth.annularity_index_definition: Fraction of Stage-1 spot cores whose Stage-2 rim value exceeds the Stage-2 core value (rim = core-component vertices with a neighbour outside the component).

specimen_scale_estimates.view: Three-quarter frontal walking pose; the torso is foreshortened and the tail is curled and only partly visible, so the body profile cannot be reconstructed photogrammetrically from this single image.
specimen_scale_estimates.torso_depth_px_estimate_note: Approximate vertical extent of the torso (back to belly) near image x = 400, estimated by eye on the 640 x 427 px image; uncertainty about +/- 15 px.
specimen_scale_estimates.tail_roi_caveat: The v2 tail ROI [410, 115, 560, 225] in mammalian_coat_markings_reference.json covers mostly the back/hindquarters and background grass; the tail is curled near x = 470-530, y = 200-240.
